name: Euler-angle rule with a Hadamard (EU′)
summary: A Z-rotation, a Hadamard and a Z-rotation equal an X–Z–X sequence of rotations, with angles given by explicit formulas.
description:
A variant of the [Euler-angle rule](../euler-angles/) in which the middle X-rotation is replaced by a Hadamard gate: $R_Z(\alpha_2)\,H\,R_Z(\alpha_1) = e^{i\gamma}R_X(\beta_3)R_Z(\beta_2)R_X(\beta_1)$, where, with $x^+=\frac{\alpha_1+\alpha_2}2$, $x^-=x^+-\alpha_2$, $z=-\sin x^+ + i\cos x^-$ and $z' = \cos x^+ - i\sin x^-$: $\beta_1=\arg z+\arg z'$, $\beta_2 = 2\arg(i+|z/z'|)$, $\beta_3=\arg z-\arg z'$ and $\gamma = x^+-\arg z+\frac{\pi-\beta_2}2$.

Vilmart showed that this rule together with the [inverse rule with a phase](../inverse-scalar-phase/) can replace the Euler-angle rule (EU), the Euler decomposition of the Hadamard and the [Clifford+T scalar rule (E)](../clifford-t-scalar/). This gives a complete axiomatisation of the universal ZX-calculus with only seven rules: spider fusion, the two identity rules, (IV), copy, bialgebra, colour change and (EU′).

The stored instance is checked for $\alpha_1=\frac\pi3$, $\alpha_2=\frac{2\pi}7$.
conditions: β₁, β₂, β₃ and γ are functions of α₁, α₂: with x⁺ = (α₁+α₂)/2, x⁻ = x⁺ − α₂, z = −sin(x⁺) + i cos(x⁻) and z′ = cos(x⁺) − i sin(x⁻), one takes β₁ = arg z + arg z′, β₂ = 2 arg(i + |z/z′|), β₃ = arg z − arg z′ and γ = x⁺ − arg z + (π − β₂)/2, with arg(0) = 0 and β₂ = 0 when z′ = 0.
notes: The build checks one generic instance of the angles; `authoring/beyond_clifford.py` additionally verifies the formulas with PyZX on random angles.
